candidates.rationale: Bad cross, flagged rather than forced. B = RANK($roa)*RANK($dollar_volume) is a 5-node tree built from two 2-node RANK(field) branches; its only complete subtrees are sizes {5,2,2,1,1}. Any child sharing >=3 nodes with B must reproduce the whole 5-node tree, which then trips the >=4-shared-subtree rejection against that same archive member. This run's own rejection log confirms it mechanically: every past crossover attempt against this exact parent (RANK($low)/(close+eps) variants, TS_MAX/TS_STD(close) variants, RANK(dollar_volume) swaps, IF_ELSE wrappers) was rejected as crossover_not_a_fusion for 'shares only 2 nodes with RANK($roa)'. No construction can clear 3. Best legal approximation: donate A's guarded dollar_volume denominator (3 nodes) intact, but invert A's numerator to close-minus-high (a retreat-from-the-high instead of recovery-off-the-low) so it isn't a bare re-normalization of A, and multiply by the largest legal piece of B, RANK($roa) alone (2 nodes, one short of the bar). Economically this asks whether high-quality names show less end-of-day give-back per unit of liquidity, but it must be reported as failing the crossover_uses_both_parents gate against B by construction.

A's liquidity-normalized recovery-off-the-low idea and B's earnings-yield idea both anchor on $close, so the fusion swaps A's dollar_volume guard for B's own guarded-close (3 nodes from B) under A's close-low numerator (3 nodes from A), producing a fresh price-relative recovery ratio, then spreads it against a bare earnings-per-share rank. This asks whether a stock's valuation rank diverges from its own recovery-off-the-low rank: cheap-but-not-recovering vs cheap-and-recovering, an interaction neither single rank states. The shared RANK($earnings_per_share) leg already co-exists with two other admitted spreads on different second legs (618d10279664fdd6, d81c79a5c4e69097), which is empirical precedent that this leg alone does not push correlation past 0.80.

Bad cross, same root cause as pair 1: A = RANK($roa)*RANK($dollar_volume) has no complete subtree of size 3 or 4 (only 5,2,2,1,1), so no child can share >=3 nodes with it without reproducing its full 5-node form and failing the archive_subtree gate against A itself. The largest legal donation is RANK($roa) alone (2 nodes), one short of the required 3. Given that ceiling, the best-effort child keeps RANK($roa) and donates B's required piece properly: B's guarded-close denominator (3 nodes) reused under a fresh numerator, $book_per_share instead of earnings_per_share, so B's own 5-node ratio and 6-node RANK wrapper are not reproduced. Economically this is a quality x book-yield composite (profitability times balance-sheet value), a coherent factor on its own merits, but it must be reported as falling short of the crossover bar for A.

candidates.rationale: A contributes its guarded-close denominator (3 nodes) as a fresh price-normalizer for B's 21-day dollar-volume delta (3 nodes, B's only legal donation), then ranks that price-adjusted flow-acceleration over its own 21-day history and multiplies by raw EPS. The fusion is a value x flow-acceleration interaction: whether trading activity is accelerating once adjusted for the stock's price level, crossed with earnings level. Neither parent alone has this: A never looks at volume flow, B never normalizes its flow measure by price or touches any valuation field.

The spread asks whether accrual quality diverges from a combined volume-acceleration/volatility-attention signal, a quality-vs-attention divergence that neither parent states: A multiplies quality by flow with no volatility term, B has no fundamental at all.

candidates.changed_node: denominator swap: TS_RANK($dollar_volume, 63) + 1e-8 replacing A's own liquidity-level denominator under A's ($high - $low) numerator
candidates.rationale: A's range numerator (3 nodes) is renormalized by B's liquidity-PERCENTILE (TS_RANK($dollar_volume,63), 3 nodes) instead of A's own liquidity-LEVEL denominator, then ranked over 21 days and multiplied by B's quality leg. This asks whether today's range is large relative to where the stock's trading activity currently sits in its own 63-day history, conditioned by ROE quality, an illiquidity-stress-relative-to-liquidity-regime measure crossed with quality that neither parent captures alone (A never touches a fundamental, B never touches range or volatility).

candidates.changed_node: new ratio $roe / ($close + 1e-8) replacing the bare RANK($roe) leg
candidates.rationale: B's guarded-close habit turns A's raw ROE level into an ROE-yield (profitability per dollar of price), which is then ranked and multiplied by A's own liquidity-percentile leg, TS_RANK($dollar_volume,63) (3 nodes, A's only legal donation). The fusion captures a valuation-flavored quality measure, profitability scaled by price, interacting with liquidity-timing: neither A's raw quality level nor B's pure price-range form expresses a price-scaled profitability signal on its own.

Both parents are pure price/volume with no fundamental leg, so the genuine fusion here is cross-domain rather than cross-asset-class: A's own-history range regime (63d, price side) times a cross-sectional rank of B's volume-instability level (TS_STD($volume,21), 3 nodes, B's only legal donation used unguarded to avoid recreating B's own guarded TS_STD($volume,21)+1e-8 denominator). This flags stocks simultaneously in an elevated own-history range regime and unusually erratic (relative to peers) trading volume, a compounding price-and-volume-stress interaction that neither parent states alone: A never touches volume, and B's own normalization is purely time-series/self-relative with no cross-sectional comparison.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: CROSSOVER. Each pair below holds two parents from DIFFERENT archive
niches. Return one child per pair that genuinely combines them.

A child must keep a complete sub-expression of at least 3 nodes
from EACH parent, checked mechanically; a child that is really just one parent
with cosmetic changes is rejected. Put both parent ids in `parent_ids`.

In the rationale, state the fusion logic: what does the combination capture that
neither parent captures alone? A conditioning variable, a normaliser, an
interaction. If you cannot name one, the pair is a bad cross and you should say
so in the rationale rather than force it.
